prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Quick clarifying question before I recommend one: by “publishes its losses” do you mean

- A) a beginner-friendly site that openly shows its own portfolio/trading performance (including losses), or  
- B) a site that plainly documents real losses in the crypto ecosystem (hacks, rug-pulls, quantified post‑mortems), or  
- C) something else?

If A (site that runs a model portfolio and publishes P&L)
- There aren’t many reputable beginners’ sites that run public live portfolios and routinely post both wins and losses in plain English. Most consumer-facing education sites avoid running an advisory portfolio for liability reasons.
- If this is essential, look at independent bloggers/newsletters who publish trade logs (search for writers on Substack who disclose performance) — but vet them carefully for conflicts.

If B (plain-English education + clear, real numbers about hacks/losses)
- Best single practical approach: pair a plain-English explainer site with a loss-postmortem data source.
  - Plain-English explainers: Coinbase Learn or Gemini Cryptopedia (beginner-friendly, clear language), plus Decrypt’s “101” series (good balance of clarity and news context).
  - Loss/post‑mortem reporting and real numbers: Rekt.news (excellent plain post‑mortems of hacks and rug pulls with dollar amounts), CertiK & Chainalysis reports (deep, quantified industry analyses), and DeFiLlama / Dune Analytics dashboards for on‑chain numbers you can inspect.
- If I had to pick one pragmatic combo for a beginner who wants plain language and real loss data: read Coinbase Learn or Decrypt for the basics, and follow Rekt.news for detailed, quantified post‑mortems of what goes wrong.

If you tell me which of A or B you mean (or give an example of what you want), I’ll give a single best site or a short tailored list.
